archetypes.pitch: Gothic, bloodthirsty and fast. Three Vampire lords and Edgar Markov build a curve nobody wants to block, and Blood tokens bridge straight into the Madness cards. For players who want a sleek, menacing aggro deck with real synergy behind it.
archetypes.rationale: Three lords plus Edgar's eminence over a deep aggressive Vampire curve; Blood tokens bridge into Madness.

archetypes.pitch: Discarding a card should cost you something; here it saves you mana. Fiery Temper and friends cast at a discount off looting and Blood tokens, and the hellbent payoffs love your empty hand. For players who enjoy reckless, fast, cost-cutting sequencing.
archetypes.rationale: Ten madness cards meet Blood tokens, looting, and escalate-discard costs; hellbent payoffs reward the empty hand.

archetypes.pitch: A tribe that simply refuses to stay dead. Gravecrawler and undying bodies recur endlessly while Gisa and Geralf and Grimgrin turn the pile into a dominant board. For players who love grinding, resilient, self-recurring armies.
archetypes.rationale: Inherently recursive tribe (Gravecrawler, undying, self-return) converted into board dominance by lords and engines.

archetypes.pitch: Flying, flash, and never quite there when the removal arrives. Mausoleum Wanderer and Spell Queller pick apart the opponent's turn while evasive Spirits run out the clock. For players who like slippery beatdown backed by counters and tricks.
archetypes.rationale: Flying flash bodies that disrupt while clocking; Tamiyo (cross-tag) draws off evasive attackers connecting.

archetypes.pitch: Creatures that punish an opponent for taking a turn off. Transforming werewolves like Huntmaster of the Fells flip into something twice the size, and the payoffs count your growing pack. For players who like beefy threats with a built-in upgrade.
archetypes.rationale: Full curve of flip werewolves plus payoffs counting Wolves and Werewolves; Garruk's Wolf tokens (cross-tag) feed those counts.

archetypes.pitch: The deepest creature pool in the cube, all pointed the same direction. Cheap Humans and token engines flood the board while Odric, Lunarch Marshal hands the whole team every keyword at once. For players who love classic go-wide aggro.
archetypes.rationale: Widest tribe: cheap bodies, two Human-token engines, Human-specific rewards (Cleaver lifelink, Mayor's anthem), Odric keyword soup.

archetypes.pitch: The deepest sacrifice deck here, where every death is worth something. The Meathook Massacre and Blood Artist drain on each one while free outlets keep the engine fed. For players who love grindy, board-eating value decks.
archetypes.rationale: Deepest cluster (59 tagged): death payoffs, free outlets, recursive fodder; Zealous Conscripts (cross-tag) turns any outlet into removal.

archetypes.pitch: Every spell gets cast twice, and your creatures are keeping count. Thing in the Ice and Docent of Perfection flip into real threats as you chain instants and sorceries out of the graveyard. For players who love spell-heavy decks and explosive payoff turns.
archetypes.rationale: Flashback doubles every spell for the count-spells payoffs; Galvanic Iteration copying Temporal Mastery (cross-tag) is the haymaker.

archetypes.pitch: A board nobody can block profitably, and then an anthem on top of it. Cathars' Crusade and Intangible Virtue make the swarm lethal, and Second Harvest simply doubles it. For players who love flooding the board and overrunning the table.
archetypes.rationale: 44 token cards feed anthem payoffs; Unnatural Growth and Decimator (cross-tag) are go-wide finishers; Tamiyo's Journal Clues are tokens for Second Harvest.

archetypes.pitch: Your graveyard is the real hand. Splinterfright and The Gitrog Monster grow off the creatures in it, and Hermit Druid plus Laboratory Maniac is a genuine combo kill. For players who like filling the bin and then cashing it in.
archetypes.rationale: Payoffs scale with creature cards in yard while a dozen enablers stock it; Hermit Druid plus Laboratory Maniac is a real win line.

archetypes.pitch: Eat your own creatures to skip several turns of mana. Emerge lets Elder Deep-Fiend and Decimator of the Provinces devour undying fodder and land on the board far ahead of schedule. For players who like a resourceful, sacrifice-fuelled ramp plan.
archetypes.rationale: Six cast-trigger Eldrazi eat undying/self-returning fodder; Heartless Summoning (cross-tag) discounts the fatties harmlessly.

archetypes.pitch: Enter-the-battlefield triggers, on repeat. Restoration Angel and Deadeye Navigator reset a board full of ETB creatures until the advantage is simply overwhelming. For players who enjoy value engines and an answer for everything.
archetypes.rationale: Four repeatable blink engines reset a cube full of ETB triggers; Helvault (fringe cross-tag) banks ETB creatures for a mass re-entry.

archetypes.pitch: Small, steady life gain that quietly becomes a win condition. Voice of the Blessed and Chalice of Life reward the drain and incidental gain your aristocrats cards were producing anyway. For players who like a resilient, grinding game plan.
archetypes.rationale: Two true gain-life payoffs over repeatable incidental gain; black drain effects double-dip.

archetypes.pitch: One creature, everything you own, one very short game. Recursive auras like Gryff's Boon dodge the usual card disadvantage and Sigarda, Host of Herons offers a target that removal cannot touch. For players who like all-in single-threat beatdown.
archetypes.rationale: Recursive/disturb auras dodge the 2-for-1; Sigarda's hexproof (cross-tag) is the ideal suit-up target.

archetypes.pitch: Land drops and dead lands both turn into cards. The Gitrog Monster and Wrenn and Seven grind value out of the yard while Cultivator Colossus is the payoff worth ramping toward. For players who love a slow, inevitable grind.
archetypes.rationale: Gitrog and Wrenn convert land drops and dead lands into cards; Cultivator Colossus is the mass payoff.

archetypes.pitch: A team that trains itself bigger with every combat. Torens makes tokens that pump one another and Hopeful Initiate spends its counters as removal. For players who like a snowballing, synergistic board.
archetypes.rationale: Torens' training tokens grow each other; Hopeful Initiate spends counters as removal; Mimic seeds any tribe.

archetypes.pitch: Giants on the battlefield several turns before anyone could cast one. Edgar's Awakening reanimates anything and Through the Breach cheats Griselbrand straight out of your hand. For players who want explosive, game-warping early plays.
archetypes.rationale: Edgar's Awakening reanimates anything; Breach cheats Griselbrand from hand; Mass Hysteria (cross-tag) gives the fatty haste. Breach does not cast, so cast-trigger Eldrazi get nothing.

archetypes.pitch: Two cards that fuse into a single monster. Gisela, the Broken Blade and Bruna, the Fading Light combine into something far past curve, and all three meld pairs are here. Since each half is perfectly playable alone, going for the meld is pure upside. For players who enjoy a rewarding two-card payoff.
archetypes.rationale: All three meld pairs and their melded faces are in the cube; each half is independently playable, so meld is pure upside.

archetypes.pitch: A combo that wins on an exact number. Tree of Perdition sets the opponent to 13 and Triskaidekaphobia finishes them on your upkeep. A spicy build-around for players who love an unusual alternate win.
archetypes.rationale: Tree sets an opponent to exactly 13; Triskaidekaphobia's upkeep trigger then wins the game outright.
